meta.notes: Contradiction searches: 'no issues' middlebox measurement, 'overhyped / not a priority', and vendor patch status. Founder-listed Entrust, DigiCert and AppViewX could not be verified: DigiCert returned a bot block and AppViewX is disallowed by robots.txt; Entrust not checked. Most bank PQC job postings (BNY, State Street, PNC via Dice/Ladders) were blocked; only Citi's own careers page was fetchable. Prospects: 21 BFSI/payments companies in the US, EU and India from their own sites; most bank leadership pages were blocked (ICICI, Rabobank, Huntington, Regions, Global Payments), so only 6 named contacts were found and none is a CISO except at Paymentology (whose size is unstated and likely below the ICP's 1000+). Sizes are only given where the company states them. Only Citi has company-specific PQC problem evidence. No source quantifies outage cost or names budgets for path-testing tools.

evidence.title: tldr.fail
evidence.quote: Due to a bug, these servers reject connections that use post-quantum cryptography, instead of negotiating classical cryptography if they do not support post-quantum cryptography.
evidence.statement: A public reference site documents servers and middleboxes that reject post-quantum TLS connections instead of falling back to classical crypto.

evidence.title: tldr.fail
evidence.quote: You may be using a vendor that has buggy servers or a buggy middlebox. You should contact your vendor and request that they patch their software.
evidence.statement: The advice to network administrators today is to contact the vendor and ask for a patch.

evidence.title: Advancing Our Amazing Bet on Asymmetric Cryptography (Google)
evidence.quote: This rollout revealed a number of previously-existing bugs in several TLS middlebox products. … The extra size from Kyber causes the TLS ClientHello to be split into two packets, resulting in a 4% median latency increase to all TLS handshakes in Chrome on desktop.
evidence.statement: Google says enabling hybrid PQ key exchange in Chrome exposed bugs in several TLS middlebox products and split the ClientHello into two packets.

evidence.title: Google Chrome's new post-quantum cryptography causes connection issues
evidence.quote: some web applications, firewalls, and servers have been dropping connections during the ClientHello TLS handshake … These issues have affected various network devices from multiple vendors, including Fortinet, SonicWall, Palo Alto Networks, and AWS
evidence.statement: After Chrome 124 enabled hybrid PQ key exchange, admins reported firewalls and servers from several vendors dropping connections.

evidence.title: Fortinet: ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR with Flow-based Deep Inspection due to ML-KEM (Known Issue)
evidence.quote: When this issue occurs, users will find that certain websites will fail to load and will present an ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR error message.
evidence.statement: On FortiGate firewalls with flow-based deep inspection, ML-KEM ClientHellos made websites fail to load for users.

evidence.title: Fortinet: ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR with Flow-based Deep Inspection due to ML-KEM (Known Issue)
evidence.quote: For precise identification, obtain a packet capture of the relevant traffic and inspect the packets in Wireshark.
evidence.statement: The vendor's diagnostic method is a manual packet capture inspected in Wireshark.

evidence.title: Fortinet: ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR with Flow-based Deep Inspection due to ML-KEM (Known Issue)
evidence.quote: According to development, the issue has been fixed starting with the following IPS Engine versions:
evidence.statement: The firewall vendor shipped fixed IPS engine builds, so this breakage was fixed by patching (the risk the idea itself names).

evidence.title: Automatic Key Exchange: post-quantum secure origin handshakes (Cloudflare)
evidence.quote: we have added the ability in the tool to check for post-quantum TLS implementation bugs. If the results come back negative, it will also try to characterize the reason for the failure. Failures often stem from legacy middleboxes, firewalls, or server buffers dropping multi-packet payloads or failing to reassemble a ClientHello split across TCP segments.
evidence.statement: Cloudflare Radar offers a free check for PQ TLS bugs and says failures often come from legacy middleboxes and firewalls dropping multi-packet ClientHellos.

evidence.title: Automatic Key Exchange: post-quantum secure origin handshakes (Cloudflare)
evidence.quote: 99.2% of post-quantum TLS 1.3 connections of the currently scanned cohort of origins now complete in a single round trip.
evidence.statement: At Cloudflare's scale, almost all PQ-capable origin connections now complete in one round trip, suggesting breakage is a small tail.

evidence.title: Automatic Key Exchange: post-quantum secure origin handshakes (Cloudflare)
evidence.quote: It is important to audit every device terminating or inspecting TLS—including load balancers, WAF appliances, and other middleboxes—to ensure X25519MLKEM768 is enabled on everything that sits between your origin and Cloudflare.

evidence.title: X25519MLKEM768 TLS 1.3 Deployment Guide (Encryption Consulting)

evidence.statement: A PQC consultancy names TLS inspection appliances rejecting the hybrid group as the most common production failure.

evidence.title: X25519MLKEM768 TLS 1.3 Deployment Guide (Encryption Consulting)

evidence.statement: For most connections, hybrid PQ key exchange already works without anyone noticing.

evidence.title: X25519MLKEM768 TLS 1.3 Deployment Guide (Encryption Consulting)
evidence.quote: Test against your real network path, including inspection appliances, before a broad rollout, and instrument negotiated-group telemetry so a middlebox problem surfaces as a metric rather than a support ticket.

evidence.title: Default PQC (ML-KEM) breaks SNI routing in Traefik

summary.statement: Today teams find PQC path breakage reactively: users see failed page loads, and the vendor-documented diagnosis is a manual packet capture inspected in Wireshark.
Public guidance tells administrators to contact their middlebox vendor for a patch, or to manually audit every TLS-terminating or inspecting device on the path.

Free point checks exist: Cloudflare Radar tests a hostname for PQ TLS bugs and characterizes failures; pqcscan reports what PQC algorithms servers advertise; inventories use nmap/sslscan or commercial discovery tools.
Ad-hoc workarounds include forcing classical curves on the client.
None of the found tools test multi-hop internal paths and pinpoint the failing hop; that gap is inferred from what the tools describe, not stated by any source.
NIST IR 8547 (final, Oct 2026) deprecates all quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms after 2030 and disallows them after 2035.
The EU roadmap asks Member States to start the transition by end-2026 and move critical infrastructure by end-2030.
PCI DSS v4.0.1 requirement 12.3.3 requires an up-to-date inventory of cipher suites and protocols in use.
In India, the RBI formed the Q-SAFE committee (May 2026), whose mandate includes a CBOM-based sector audit; CERT-In's BOM guidelines cover CBOM. Neither sets a binding bank deadline yet.
Against this: for commercial firms deprecation means documented risk acceptance, not a ban, and in 2025 only 5% of ISACA respondents called quantum a high near-term priority while 41% had no plans.
At Citi, PQC readiness is an enterprise program inside Cybersecurity & Technology Risk, with a program lead fielding rising regulatory requests.
Budget is a hurdle: a former bank CISO says unquantified migrations do not get funded, and an Indian vendor says BFSI funding for quantum prep remains low.
No evidence found on who signs for network-path testing tools specifically (security vs network teams) or on budgets in the $30k-$150k range.
When the hybrid ClientHello breaks a middlebox, websites fail to load; Chrome's rollout exposed bugs in several middlebox products from multiple vendors.
The most common production failure is a TLS inspection appliance rejecting the hybrid group; reverse proxies that sniff SNI from the first packet also misroute.
At scale the failures are a tail: Cloudflare reports 99.2% of PQ origin connections completing in one round trip, and a deployment guide says it is invisible for most connections.
No source quantifies outage hours, incident cost or staff time per incident.

Commercial cryptographic inventory platforms already include network discovery: Keyfactor AgileSec (network traffic sensors), SandboxAQ AQtive Guard, IBM Quantum Safe, Encryption Consulting CBOM Secure.
Free and open-source options exist for CBOM generation (CBOMkit) and PQC endpoint scanning (pqcscan, Cloudflare Radar).
NGFWs such as Palo Alto can detect and log PQC use; consultancies sell middlebox-aware rollout planning.
Large banks track vendor PQC roadmaps in Confluence and Jira.
Guidance favours testing the real network path including inspection appliances before rollout, and negotiated-group telemetry rather than overall handshake success.
Fallback connections should be reported separately from PQ-protected ones.
The durable fix is a vendor patch, and at least one major firewall vendor shipped fixed builds, which limits the long-term value of breakage-only diagnostics.
No buyer statement was found on whether a proxy/fallback product is wanted.
CDN-provided PQC covers only the edge, not origin, internal APIs or service-to-service traffic.
Inspecting firewalls on decrypted paths strip PQC from the ClientHello, silently downgrading that hop to classical crypto.
Service-mesh PQ policies apply datacenter-wide with no per-service canary; a telecom participant at the IETF expects PQ-blocking middleboxes in internal networks into 2030-2035.
No practitioner first-person evidence was found about east-west PQC breakage at a bank.

current_solutions.statement: Breakage is found reactively (failed page loads) and diagnosed by packet capture in Wireshark, then fixed by vendor patches or by forcing classical crypto.
For external endpoints, free checks exist (Cloudflare Radar, pqcscan), and CDNs fall back to classical automatically.
Cryptographic inventories are built with commercial discovery platforms (Keyfactor, SandboxAQ, IBM, Encryption Consulting) or free scanners and CBOMkit.
Large banks run PQC as a governance program, tracking vendor roadmaps in Jira and Confluence.
